what_it_does: Addresses the memory bottleneck in large language model inference by scaling processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures—chips where computation happens directly in the memory system rather than shuttling data to distant processors. The multi-chiplet approach handles sparse weight matrices by breaking them into irregular patterns, routes computations through a switching network to distribute work across memory arrays, and stacks memory vertically while using separate packaging chiplets to minimize long-distance communication, enabling efficient inference on models with 70 billion or more parameters.
